turns.doctor_question: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Hi, Doctor. Thank you for seeing me. Um, I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time. 

I guess I'm here because... well, things have been a bit complicated at my job lately. I'm a transportation inspector, and I always try really hard to do things by the book. I actually just won a county safety award recently, which I was really proud of. But... ever since I got it, it's like certain people at work have been, I don't know, twisting my inspection reports? 

They keep asking these really pointed budget questions, almost like they're trying to make me look crooked. I mean, is it normal to feel upset about something like that? My supervisor keeps saying it's just a standard, normal review, and I really don't want to sound like a complainer or like I'm causing trouble, but... I can just tell there's a coordinated effort to discredit me. I just want to figure out how to handle it so I can keep doing a good job. Does that make sense for why I'm here?

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient expresses a fixed belief that coworkers are coordinating an effort to discredit them, despite their supervisor's reassurance that it is just a standard review.

top_partial.disease_name: Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

turns.doctor_question: During this stressful time, have you ever heard voices or sounds when no one was around?
turns.patient_response:
Oh, um... no. No, definitely not. I've never experienced anything like that. 

I mean, I know I'm really stressed out right now, but my mind is completely clear. I'm just hearing what people are actually saying in the office, you know? I hope I didn't make it sound like I was... well, losing touch with reality or anything. I'm just trying to deal with a tough situation at work, but I'm definitely not hearing things that aren't there. I'm doing okay otherwise, I promise. Does that make sense?

symptom_reasoning.S020: The patient explicitly denies hearing voices or sounds that are not there, stating they have never experienced anything like that.

turns.doctor_question: Have you found yourself feeling like people were untrustworthy or trying to undermine you in other areas of your life, or in past jobs?
turns.patient_response:
Oh, um... no. No, definitely not. I've always gotten along really well with my coworkers at past jobs. I really pride myself on being a good team player, you know? 

Outside of work, everything is totally fine, too. I don't have any issues with my friends or anything like that. It's really just... just this one specific situation right now, ever since that award. 

I really hope I don't sound like, um, like a difficult person who just complains everywhere they go, or like I think everyone is out to get me. I'm really not like that at all. I always try to see the best in people and just keep my head down and do good work. Is it okay that I'm just focusing on this one work thing? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information and not making it seem worse than it is.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient confirms that their feelings of being undermined are focused entirely on 'this one specific situation right now, ever since that award,' maintaining their specific persecutory delusion.
symptom_reasoning.S072: The patient denies having pervasive negative beliefs about others, stating they 'always try to see the best in people' and do not think everyone is out to get them.
symptom_reasoning.S075: The patient denies social detachment or isolation, stating that outside of work everything is fine and they 'don't have any issues with my friends.'

turns.doctor_question: How long has this coordinated effort against you at work been going on?
turns.patient_response:
Well, um... I guess it's been about a year now. Yeah, right around a year. 

It started right after I got recognized for that county safety initiative I mentioned. Before that, everything was perfectly fine, and I thought I was doing a really good job of making everyone happy. But then... well, it's just been this slow build over the last twelve months of them questioning my reports and making those little comments. 

I hope it doesn't sound like I'm holding onto a grudge for too long or anything. I've really tried to just brush it off and be a good sport for the whole year, I promise. I just... I finally felt like I needed to talk to someone about it because I want to make sure I'm handling it the right way. Is a year a normal amount of time to try and work through something like this on your own?

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient confirms a year-long belief that coworkers are engaged in a coordinated effort against them, which is indicative of persecutory delusions.
